title: Unseen Vivienne Westwood photos show 'born protester'

input.summary: Images of the fashion icon's fracking protest show "the reality of her", Paul Wolfgang Webster says

title: Manchester woman tackling taboos of childlessness and miscarriage

input.lead: Connie Kerr used to dread being asked if she was a mum.
input.summary: Connie Kerr used to dread being asked if she was a mum. Now she is breaking the stigma with her truth
input.evidence_text: For years, that was the question Connie Kerr dreaded Connie, from Manchester, said she had done "all the right things". She had a successful career, a husband and assumed children would follow But after four miscarriages in the space of two years, the future she imagined for herself was taken away She said she was reminded daily of what she had lost. From television adverts to workplace small talk, Connie felt everything reinforced the message that a woman without children was somehow incomplete More than a decade later, she has turned her experiences into a play and hopes to challenge the taboos that still surround childlessness, miscarriage and infertility Connie spoke to BBC News ahead of Baby Loss Awareness Week about why she wants to encourage conversations about a subject she believes is still taboo

title: Macbeth to be staged at Oldham's last nightclub Liquid and Envy

input.lead: Shakespeare's famous play will be performed at the nightclub in an effort to engage "new audiences"
input.summary: Shakespeare's famous play will be performed at the nightclub in an effort to engage "new audiences"
input.evidence_text: While the Oldham Coliseum Theatre's doors remain closed during its major revamp, the creative team has needed to think outside the box when deciding where to temporarily decamp They have chosen the last remaining nightclub in the Greater Manchester town to stage William Shakespeare's Macbeth "I want to blow the dust off Shakespeare," said the Coliseum's new creative director Nick Bagnall "This isn't about putting the play on a pedestal, it's about creating an experience that grabs people by the throat, whether they have seen Macbeth 10 times or never encountered it before "We want people who have never set foot in a theatre to walk into Liquid and Envy and feel this story belongs to them "Staging Macbeth inside a working Oldham nightclub creates its own intrigue."

title: Warning to drivers as part of Bury M60 to shut again

input.lead: Severe congestion is expected while work takes place at Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
input.summary: Severe congestion is expected while work takes place at Simister Island on the M60 in Bury
input.evidence_text: Warning to drivers as part of Bury M60 to shut again - BBC News Image caption, Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday evening By Lynette Horsburgh North West Published 9 October 2026 Updated 10 October 2026 Drivers are being warned of "severe congestion" when a busy stretch of motorway is closed this weekend as part of an upgrade to the road. Junction 17 and 18 of the M60 in Bury, Greater Manchester, will be shut on Saturday night until 06:00 on Monday. The closures are to enable the demolition of two large overhead gantries at the Simister Island Interchange. It comes after two others were removed last month. National Highways said the work was part of a £300m improvement scheme and would improve traffic flow, support future housing, employment and growth across the region. Frances Oliver, of National Highways, told BBC North West Tonight : "These gantries are up to 120 tonnes so it's very similar to removing a small footbridge so it is quite a large amount of work for us to undertake." Image caption, Two busy junctions at Simister and Prestwich will be closed for the work Oliver added: "We are expecting there to be severe congestion in the area so we are asking people to plan their journeys, check before they travel and if at all try not to travel or defer their journey. "The message is if you don't need to be in the area please try not to be." Begging at some of the region's busiest junction But it seems to have become more common in recent months, across more of the region's roads. Those involved are often putting themselves at risk People are regularly seen walking past queues of traffic asking for money, or sitting at traffic islands between hectic crossroads. It's a heartbreaking sight that comes at a time when the government is pushing to eradicate rough sleeping It's understood that police who work supporting vulnerable people in Greater Manchester believe the increase is partly down to the repeal of the historic Vagrancy Act - which dated back to 1824 - in June this year. That move officially decriminalised begging and rough sleeping in But there is also an understanding that begging on major roads, while drivers often face long queues of traffic, is believed to be more lucrative than in other places. Effectively, people in tough situations are willing to take the risk to their personal safety

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

input.lead: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing.
input.summary: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised
input.evidence_text: Tech investment isn't slowing down, but the pattern of investment is changing. As investors grow increasingly selective, the capital ecosystem has become polarised. More capital is being concentrated in fewer companies while the market for exits remains difficult Financial news recently added another dimension to that discussion. AI-related shares fell last week after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei called for a slower approach to the development of increasingly capable AI models. Nvidia finished the day down 3.4%, SoftBank fell 10.7% in Tokyo Additionally, the Bank of England is predicted to increase interest rates later this year, which could affect the North West's tech funding landscape by raising the cost of capital across the board, compressing valuations, pushing investors toward profitability over growth-at-all The British Business Bank's 2026 Small Business Equity Tracker found that equity investment into UK smaller businesses fell 4% to £12.3bn in 2025. Seed deal numbers fell 27% and venture deals fell 13%. AI companies attracted 44% of all investment into smaller businesses while the Beauhurst recorded £14.4bn of UK equity investment across 2,799 deals in the first half of 2026 but three AI companies accounted for 29% of all the capital raised. Those very large rounds can make the overall market look stronger than it feels to businesses raising at seed or Ser Beauhurst's analysis shows that UK equity investment more than doubled between 2017 and 2021 to £32.2bn while annual exits remained at around 400 to 500. An exit takes a median of four years from a funding round
